name: John Hancock
fact: President of the Continental Congress; signed his name largest, famously so 'King George can read it without his spectacles.'
context: As Congress's president, Hancock signed first and alone on July 4 -- most other delegates didn't sign the engrossed copy until August 2, 1776.

name: Benjamin Franklin
fact: Oldest signer at 70; also signed the Treaty of Paris and the Constitution.
context: He's the only Founder to have signed all four pivotal documents of the era: the Declaration, the Treaty of Alliance with France, the Treaty of Paris, and the Constitution.

name: John Adams
fact: Became the second President of the United States.
context: He served on the five-man drafting committee with Jefferson and pushed hard for independence on the floor of Congress, even though he wasn't the one who wrote the final text.

name: Thomas Jefferson
fact: Principal author of the Declaration; became the third President.
context: He was only 33 when he wrote it, and later asked that his tombstone credit him as its author, along with founding the University of Virginia -- not as President.

name: Samuel Adams
fact: Organized the Boston Tea Party; cousin of John Adams.
context: He'd spent nearly two decades agitating against British policy before independence was even on the table -- by 1776 he was one of the most wanted men in the colonies.

name: Roger Sherman
fact: Only person to sign all four founding documents: the Declaration, Articles of Association, Articles of Confederation, and the Constitution.
context: He also proposed the Connecticut Compromise (Great Compromise) at the 1787 convention, which created the House and Senate split that still defines Congress.

name: Elbridge Gerry
fact: Later Vice President under Madison; namesake of 'gerrymandering.'
context: The term comes from an 1812 Massachusetts redistricting map drawn under his governorship, shaped like a salamander -- press cartoonists coined 'Gerry-mander' and it stuck.

name: Richard Henry Lee
fact: Introduced the resolution calling for independence on June 7, 1776.
context: His resolution -- 'these United Colonies are, and of right ought to be, free and independent States' -- is what actually triggered Jefferson being asked to draft the Declaration.

name: George Wythe
fact: First American law professor; mentor to Thomas Jefferson.
context: He held the first chair of law at an American college, at William & Mary, and also taught John Marshall, who became the pivotal early Chief Justice of the Supreme Court.

name: Caesar Rodney
fact: Rode all night through a thunderstorm to cast Delaware's deciding vote for independence.
context: He was suffering from cancer at the time and rode roughly 80 miles overnight to break a tied Delaware delegation just in time for the vote.

name: Button Gwinnett
fact: Died in a duel in 1777; his signature is among the rarest and most valuable in history.
context: Because he died so soon after signing, authenticated Gwinnett signatures are extraordinarily scarce -- among the most expensive autographs in the world when they surface.

name: Lyman Hall
fact: A physician who later became Governor of Georgia.
context: He was one of only three delegates from Georgia, a colony that almost didn't send anyone to the Second Continental Congress at all.

name: William Whipple
fact: A former sea captain and slave trader who later freed his own slave.
context: He freed the man he had enslaved, Prince Whipple, reportedly after Prince pointed out the contradiction of fighting a war for liberty while enslaving people.
